title: Even unimodular ideal lattices of rank 88 over Q(zeta_115): note, addendum, data, programs and verifications (version 1.4: X(P1151 sigma24) and the candidate X(P461 sigma91))
description:
Note, addendum, data, programs and verification records on even unimodular ideal lattices of rank 88 over the cyclotomic field L = Q(zeta_115). The note is given in English (article/rang88_en.pdf, a translation) and in its original French (article/rang88.pdf).

Note. The set S of classes of unimodular ideal lattices over L is in bijection with the class group of L, which is cyclic of order h-(115) = 44 697 909; it splits into 508 463 Galois orbits. Sakamoto's two extremal lattices lie in the principal orbit and in the unique non-trivial 3-torsion orbit. Two ideal lattices over L with minimum at least 8 are isometric if and only if their classes are Galois conjugate. A gluing construction is extended to non-principal ideals, and a finite extremality criterion is derived from a Parseval-type inequality. The orbits of eight prime ideals are rejected by explicit vectors of norm 6. For two prime ideals of degree 2, above 139 and 599, the lattices X139 and X599 are extremal: their minimum 8 is established by a computer-assisted proof, with an explicit execution model, and the computations were replicated on a second computer. They are isometric neither to each other nor to Sakamoto's lattices, without assuming GRH.

Addendum (version 1.1). Two further extremal lattices, X4969 and X4049 (computer-assisted minimum, each side swept twice on two rented machines with byte-identical receipts); extremality is not an invariant of the twin pairs of the sigma24 layer; a description of the orbits of that layer without GRH.

Version 1.2. Norm-6 witnesses of the rejections in the addendum, with two independent checkers (PARI/GP and pure Python).

Version 1.3. English translation of the note and updated French text (status of the non-isometry without GRH; normalizers of the multiplication group of orders 460 and 920 in Aut(X139) and Aut(X599)); archive metadata. No new computation.

Version 1.4. Timestamped data for two further even unimodular ideal lattices of rank 88, attached to products of two primes of degree 1 swapped by a Galois automorphism (folder v14_P1151s24_et_candidat_P461s91/): one extremal lattice and one CANDIDATE. X(P1151sigma24), with I = (1151, zeta - 6)(1151, zeta - 605): computer-assisted minimum 8 (exhaustive sweep of both sides of the criterion, no touch), run twice on two different machines with identical canonical fingerprints of the receipts; its class is not Galois conjugate to those of the six known extremal lattices, without assuming GRH. X(P461sigma91), a CANDIDATE, with I = (461, zeta - 5)(461, zeta - 115): exhaustive sweep of both sides without touch on a single machine, not replicated (one side resumed from an interrupted launch; only the short part of the receipts is cross-checked, against those of P461sigma24); minimum 8 claimed by the authors; non-isometric to X139, X599, X4969, X4049, X(P1151sigma24) and LS without assuming GRH, and to L0 only under GRH. The note and the addendum are unchanged.

Status: the minimum 8 of the new lattices is computer-assisted (execution model M1, M2, H1-H3 stated in the note); it is not a formal proof. X(P461sigma91) is a candidate: the sweep has not been replicated and the minimum is only claimed. Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) and Astra (OpenAI) assisted the author; they are not authors.
